title: Speciation, Extinction and Biodiversity
seo_title: Speciation and Extinction Worksheets: Isolation, New Species and Biodiversity (Biology)
standard_text: Evaluate the evidence supporting claims that changes in environmental conditions may result in: (1) increases in the number of individuals of some species, (2) the emergence of new species over time, and (3) the extinction of other species. Create or revise a simulation to test a solution to mitigate adverse impacts of human activity on biodiversity.
meta_desc: Free high school biology worksheets on speciation, extinction and biodiversity (NGSS HS-LS4-5, HS-LS4-6): isolation, environmental change, population data and simulations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Change can grow, create or end species.
key_sub: Isolation leads to new species; species that cannot adapt go extinct.
body_html:
How to think about it

Environmental change can grow, create or end species.

  • Some species increase when a change gives them resources.
  • Isolation (geographic, behavioral, temporal, mechanical) stops interbreeding; over many generations a new species can form.
  • Species that cannot adapt fast enough go extinct. Simulations help test solutions that protect biodiversity.
Example

A river splits squirrels into two groups. Which isolation?

A physical barrier

Answer: geographic

Example

Bees: 1,200 → 900. Percent drop?

300 ÷ 1,200 × 100

Answer: 25%

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a new species forms in one generation.
  • Thinking a change affects every species the same way.
  • Thinking extinction only happened to dinosaurs.

faq.q: How does a new species form?
faq.a: A population is split by isolation. Over many generations, the groups change differently until they can no longer interbreed.

faq.q: What can happen to species when the environment changes?
faq.a: Some species increase, some evolve into new species and some go extinct.

faq.q: How do simulations help protect biodiversity?
faq.a: They let scientists compare solutions, such as corridors or catch limits, with a no-action control before trying them in the real world.

items.q: Can an environmental change help some species while harming others?
